key_insight: Adapting only the Transformer layers that are least similar to their inputs can improve task-specific gains while better preserving a model’s general capabilities.
engineering_relevance: LS-LoRA offers a simple, forward-only way to target fine-tuning where it matters, reducing capability drift without needing extra replay data or explicit regularization.
method: Measure layer sensitivity using empirical Fisher information.
Use input–output cosine similarity as a cheap proxy to rank layers by sensitivity.
Insert trainable LoRA adapters only into low-similarity layers.
evidence_signal: Across mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks, LS-LoRA improved average target-task performance and retained more commonsense reasoning ability than standard all-layer LoRA.
watch_item: Input–output similarity is only a proxy for Fisher sensitivity, so layer ranking may be model- and task-dependent and should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Where to Adapt Matters: Layer-Selective Fine-Tuning for Capability Retention
